widgets_values:
HOW THIS WORKFLOW WORKS

1) Pass 1 runs low-resolution fractional V2V to transfer motion and timing from the source clip while replacing the performers using the reference images.

2) The de-rope stage analyzes the pass-1 output and source video/audio, builds smear guidance, and prepares a cleaner latent for the second pass.

3) The latent is upscaled 1.5x, then Pass 2 performs a short high-resolution refinement.

4) H3ExactRecover restores exact source-frame timing, and the original source audio is reused for the final output.

The two VHS outputs preview/save both the pre-recover comparison output and the final recovered output.

widgets_values:
FRACTIONAL MASK NOTE

global_strength determines how much the source video that is encoded into the latent will get denoised. 1 means it gets fully denoised, 0 means it doesnt get denoised at all. so a value close to 1 means it will almost completely get denoised, but not quite.

global_strength = 0.9995 is intentional. It leaves a very faint residue of the source video inside the target latent. That residue helps anchor choreography and motion transfer, giving the model a subtle motion guide while still replacing identity and appearance.

For the best results I suggest you try global_strength values between 0.995 and 0.9997 (the highest possible value before 1.0) for motion transfer. It should be high enough so the source video will pick up on the prompt and references to switch or change characters or objects, but as low as possible so the latent residue helps guide the motion in the generated clip. Finetuning this value for your specific clip will yield the best results.

UPDATE 9 — PRECISION
Mask strength is fractional, not infinitely continuous. The compatibility token grid uses ceil(value*4096)/4096: 0.9995 → 0.99951171875; 0.9997 → 0.999755859375; 0.9998 → 1.0 (fully generative). Tiny slider changes can share one grid value. Native support may use finer precision. Keep BasicScheduler denoise at 1.0. PR #15988 velocity correction is checked lazily when masked nodes run; a native fix is never applied twice. Source videos must be constant 24 fps.

CHUNKED FEED-FORWARD NOTE

With the default settings the second pass runs at 1920x1056 for almost 5 seconds with de-rope (which can increase the frame count 3 or 4 fold). The KJNodes MiniMax Chunk Feed-Forward patch is used here to reduce peak memory during this high-resolution refinement.
